=== FINDING 1 (BLOCKING): the generated HANDOFF block is one proof record behind, so lwb-check-state-claims fails on this head ===
Measured at df9ce2e:
  $ python3 scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .   -> exit 1
  FAIL: HANDOFF.md:54: [stale deliverable proof state in generated block]
        recorded=['22/22 proven', ...] re-derived=['23/23 proven', ...]
This is the ordering trap, inside a single commit. df9ce2e's own message says the block was regenerated 'in the SAME commit as the proof record' to avoid moving the reviewable head -- the intent is right and the commit does contain both writes, but scripts/lwb_handoff.py --write ran BEFORE proof/52.json existed on disk, so the count it derived (22) is one behind the 23 records the commit actually ships. The diff shows it plainly: HANDOFF.md's Generated timestamp, main SHA and Session lines all changed in df9ce2e while the '22/22 proven' line did not.
Why it blocks: .github/workflows/ci.yml's `test` job runs `python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .`. Real CI agrees with my local run -- `test` is a failure on all six matrix legs of df9ce2e (ubuntu/macos/windows x 3.10/3.12), while every `check` leg, lwb-portable and lwb-foreign-repo leg is green.
Not pre-existing, and not a stale-origin/main artifact: I fetched origin/main (6afc545) FIRST, and this branch's recorded main SHA 6afc545 matches live main exactly, so the main-SHA claim is fine. On origin/main itself the same command exits 0 ('lwb-check-state-claims check passed'). The failure is derived from proof/ in the working tree, not from main.
Fair to the PR body: its 'What I ran' list claims state_claims passed. That was TRUE when written -- I ran it at the earlier commit ad92d5e and it exits 0 there (24 files in proof/, 22 deliverable records). The regression arrived with df9ce2e. The claim is stale, not fabricated.
Fix, reproduced: re-run `python scripts/lwb_handoff.py --write` now that proof/52.json exists. I did that in a scratch copy; the block became '23/23 proven' and state_claims exited 0. Restored the file afterwards -- I changed nothing on this branch but the file this record is.

=== FINDING 2 (non-blocking, design): the rule consults repo facts it never uses, which silently disables it entirely on the Codex plugin ===
evaluate() returns None when event.repo is None or repo.facts_incomplete is True. But this rule consumes NO repo fact for its decision: classification reads only event.tool_input, authorisation only config.options -- the module docstring says so itself ('a presence/completeness gate, not a field this rule consumes'). So that gate is not honest abstention, it is a kill-switch.
Measured, in DENY mode, command 'git push --force origin main':
  repo facts present      -> permit=False, finding raised
  repo is None            -> permit=True, no finding
  facts_incomplete=True   -> permit=True, no finding
And end-to-end through the SHIPPED vendor hooks (I patched nothing in core for this; I drove the real plugin entrypoints, per the vendor/core trap):
  plugins/claude/lwb/bin/lwb_hook.py -> warns, naming options.allow.force_push
  plugins/codex/lwb/bin/lwb_hook.py  -> 'reporting only, no policy enforced yet' and NOTHING else
Same command, same rule, same policy; one plugin gates it, the other is silent. Root cause: adapters/codex/hook_io.py builds its Event with no repo= argument at all, so repo is always None there. The Codex vendor tree ships this rule and core/policy/default.json enables it, so the Codex plugin advertises a destructive-action gate that can never fire. At 'warn' nobody notices; when a later build-plan item arms it to deny, it will deny on Claude and permit everything on Codex.
The docstring justifies the silence by citing this repo's own defect pattern -- 'could not check must never share a representation with checked, found nothing'. For lwb_proof_required that reasoning holds, and I verified why: it genuinely reads repo.proof_ids and repo.branch, so without facts it has no evidence. Here the reasoning inverts: the evidence (the command string) was fully available and WAS classified, and the rule then throws that away and returns the identical representation -- None -- that it returns for 'no destructive action here'. That is the very conflation the comment invokes, committed by the code the comment defends. I am NOT asking for repo facts to be gathered in Codex; the narrow point is that this rule's decision does not need them, so the gate should be dropped or the inertness surfaced rather than silent.

=== FINDING 3 (non-blocking, under-match): '-n' means --no-verify for git commit, and skips the whole segment ===
_segments() drops any segment containing a token in lwb_proof_required's _NON_PUBLISHING_FLAGS ('--dry-run', '-n', '--help', '-h'), reused verbatim. For 'git push' that is correct ('-n' is --dry-run). For 'git commit' it is not: '-n' is --no-verify. Measured, DENY mode, repo facts present:
  'git commit --amend'              -> CAUGHT
  'git commit --amend --no-verify'  -> CAUGHT
  'git commit --amend -n'           -> MISSED
  'git commit -n --amend'           -> MISSED
  'git push --force origin main -n' -> MISSED (correct: a real dry run)
So the spelling that also skips the hooks is the one that escapes, and the flag's meaning is subcommand-dependent while the check is applied across all subcommands. Consistent with the declared under-match bias, but it is not in the docstring's named blind-spot list.

=== FINDING 4 (non-blocking, documentation completeness): three destructive shapes missed that the named blind-spot list does not name ===
The docstring commits to a standard -- 'Every blind spot below is accepted and named, not left to be found later as a bug' -- and lists force-push gaps as only 'git -C', env-prefixed, 'git.exe', and script/alias. Measured misses beyond that list:
  'git push origin +main:main'  -> MISSED  (the classic '+refspec' force-push; not a listed gap)
  'git push --mirror origin'    -> MISSED  (can delete remote refs)
  'git push --prune origin'     -> MISSED  (deletes remote refs absent locally)
For contrast, correctly MISSED-and-named: 'gh api -X DELETE repos/o/r/git/refs/heads/x', which the docstring does explicitly name. Not a correctness bug given the under-match posture; it is a gap against the PR's own naming standard.
